issues.description: State machine collapsed from three states to two, complecting 'discovered' and 'in-progress' into one 'walking' label
issues.detail: The prior design separated working (children being pushed) from walking (cycle detection during push). Merging them into walking removes a distinction the push() switch still relies on. The name now describes two different temporal phases of the same node. Either keep both states with clearer names, or document why one suffices.

issues.description: Cleanup-on-defer complects iterator lifetime with sorter identity and hides a place-oriented reset
issues.detail: Moving clear(state) and stack truncation into the defer entangles 'when iteration ends' with 'when state is valid.' If yield panics or the caller abandons the iter mid-stream, the Sorter's mutable places are left in an ambiguous condition. A pure reset at Sort entry is simpler: one identity, one explicit time of reset.

issues.description: Yield-failure path now leaves node marked walking instead of sorted, changing the value semantics of an interrupted sort
issues.detail: Previously s.state[k] = sorted ran unconditionally after pop. Now it only runs when yield succeeds. If the consumer stops early and the Sorter is reused (state cleared on defer), this is fine — but the two facts (cleanup-on-defer, conditional marking) are now coupled across distant lines. The invariant should be stated, not implied.

issues.description: s.stack = s.stack[0:] removal is correct but the replacement clear+truncate pair is doing two things at once
issues.detail: clear(s.stack) zeroes elements (for GC of Node references); s.stack = s.stack[:0] resets length. Both are needed, but the comment in the PR description ('non-zero elements in the stack slice') is the only place this intent is recorded. The code itself does not say why clear precedes truncate. One line of comment would make the time-and-value story explicit.

issues.description: Comment typos ('visisted', 'if its') degrade the one place the state machine is explained
issues.detail: The rewritten comment is now the canonical description of the two-visit DFS state model — and it contains 'visisted' and 'if its' (should be 'it's'). Since the state machine just lost a state, this comment is doing more load-bearing work than before. Worth a clean pass.

review.summary: This change is mostly a sensible move toward simpler reset semantics — one place that clears state (the defer) instead of two — but it pays for that with new complecting elsewhere. The three-state machine (unsorted/working/walking/sorted) collapses to two, and the push() cycle-detection branch now reuses 'walking' to mean two distinct things in time. The conditional s.state[k] = sorted assignment couples cleanup correctness to defer ordering across thirty lines. The essential algorithm — DFS with two visits per node — is unchanged; what shifted is where the values, the identity (the Sorter), and the time of reset live. Worth tightening the state-machine naming and adding one comment that states the reuse invariant explicitly.
